summary: The article argues the New York Yankees, coming off a poor 2023 season, should not trade second baseman Gleyber Torres despite talk of cutting the roughly $300 million budget. It cites his 2023 stats, his projected $15.3 million salary, Miami Marlins interest, and the team's thin second-base options. The author concludes that losing Torres would deepen the team's hitting and depth problems.
one_line: An Essentially Sports opinion piece argues the Yankees should keep Gleyber Torres rather than trade him to cut spending before 2024.
key_facts: The New York Mets and New York Yankees both missed the 2023 playoffs and were scrutinized as the league's highest spenders.
The Yankees had their worst finish in seven years in 2023.
The Yankees are reportedly considering cutting down the $300 million budget for the 2024 season.
Gleyber Torres is 26 years old and avoided arbitration before 2023 by signing a $9.95 million contract.
In 2023 Torres scored 90 runs, hit 25 home runs and had 68 RBIs, with an average of 0.273, an OPS of 0.800 and an OBP of 0.347.
Torres finished second on the team in fielding behind Anthony Volpe, with 80 double plays, 563 chances and a 0.975 fielding percentage.
According to mlbtraderumors.com, Torres is expected to earn $15.3 million next year, so trading him could save the Yankees money.
The Miami Marlins have been interested in Torres for a long time.
Earlier in the offseason, a possible third-party audit of the Yankees was discussed and later dropped, and Aaron Judge's comments drew attention to conflicts and divisions within the core four.
The article says Torres is the sole second base option; replacing him could mean moving Oswaldo Peraza from third base to second, though Peraza struggled this season.
Free agents Whit Merrifield and Adam Frazier have not done well, per the article.
The Yankees finished second last in total hits and had over 1400 strikeouts, while Torres has a 14.6% strikeout rate.
Brian Cashman is described as pressing a reboot button for a better 2024.
